content.text: All renewal terms sit at the preferred position. No redline needed.

input.quote: 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.
input.rationale: Renewal is automatic but fully meets our preferred checklist: each renewal term is twelve months (§ 8.2), Customer may opt out on thirty days' written notice (§ 8.2, i.e. within our 30-day maximum and well inside the 60-day fallback window), Vendor must send a renewal reminder at least sixty days beforehand (§ 8.2, with the opt-out deadline extended if the reminder is missed — a mechanic that favours us), and renewal uplift is capped at the lesser of CPI over the preceding twelve months and three percent (§ 8.3). Because every conditional automatic-renewal element is satisfied, no mutual-written-agreement requirement is needed. § 8.1's three-year initial term and its take-or-pay interaction are a minimum-commitment issue, not a renewal issue, and are not flagged here. No deviation; no redline proposed.

mappings.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
